test_title: PYST 69: RRB Group D - Mathematics (Held On: 27 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: In an election with two candidates, 25% of the total votes were invalid. One candidate received 40% of the valid votes. If the total number of votes was 3,75,000, how many valid votes did the other candidate receive?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total votes = 375000

Valid votes = 75% ⇒ 375000 × 0.75 = 281250

One candidate = 40% ⇒ other = 60%

Other candidate votes = 60% of 281250

**∴ Answer = 168750**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total votes = 375000

Invalid votes = 25%

One candidate gets 40% of valid votes

**Formula used:**

Valid votes = Total votes × (100 − invalid%) ÷ 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Valid votes = 375000 × 75 ÷ 100 = 281250

⇒ Votes of one candidate = 40% of 281250

⇒ Votes of other candidate = 60% of 281250

⇒ = 281250 × 60 ÷ 100

⇒ = 168750

**∴ The correct answer is 168750.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Valid Votes Concept

Valid votes = Total votes − Invalid votes

Percentage Split

If one part is x%, other part = (100 − x)%

Basic Percentage

x% of number = (x ÷ 100) × number

Quick Trick

Always convert percentages to fractions for faster calculation
